candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — educate client about medications and review pertinent medication-related data; integrated reproductive-health teaching
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antiseizure medication planning before pregnancy
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with epilepsy who are planning pregnancy to seek preconception antiseizure-medication review and to discuss guideline-recommended folic acid supplementation rather than changing therapy independently.

options.A: Stop the antiseizure medication independently before conception because all antiseizure medications have the same fetal-risk profile.
options.B: Arrange preconception review so seizure control and medication-specific fetal risks can be optimized, and discuss recommended folic acid supplementation with the clinician.
options.C: Continue the regimen without preconception discussion because pregnancy does not affect antiseizure-medication treatment decisions.
options.D: Avoid folic acid because supplementation is contraindicated for people who take antiseizure medications.

candidate.rationale: The 2024 AAN/AES/SMFM guideline recommends optimizing antiseizure medication choice and dose for both seizure control and fetal outcomes at the earliest possible opportunity before conception. It also recommends at least 0.4 mg of folic acid daily before conception and during pregnancy for people with epilepsy who take an antiseizure medication. B is therefore the best teaching. A falsely treats all medications as equivalent and encourages unsupervised treatment change, C omits recommended preconception optimization, and D contradicts the guideline's folic-acid recommendation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For people with epilepsy of childbearing potential, antiseizure therapy should be optimized for seizure control and fetal outcomes as early as possible before conception, and folic acid supplementation of at least 0.4 mg/day is recommended before and during pregnancy.
candidate.source_document_title: Teratogenesis, Perinatal, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes After In Utero Exposure to Antiseizure Medication: Practice Guideline From the AAN, AES, and SMFM
candidate.source_locator: Major recommendations in abstract/clinician guidance — optimize ASM and dose preconceptionally; prescribe at least 0.4 mg folic acid daily preconceptionally and during pregnancy
candidate.source_organization: American Academy of Neurology (AAN), American Epilepsy Society (AES), and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM)
candidate.source_version_date: Practice Guideline May 2024; Neurology publication June 2024; current AAN guideline page rechecked 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: A client with epilepsy who takes an antiseizure medication is planning pregnancy. Which teaching is most appropriate?
